name: fsevents_parse
description: Read /.fseventsd record files: the per-volume change log, gzip (one or more members) holding pages of 1SLD or 2SLD records. Returns (files in the order their names are printed, the withheld ones in an order that is new every run) each path with its event id, raw and decoded flags, node id (2SLD only) and where in the file it was (gzip member, page and record offsets in the decompressed stream), and the log's own identity from fseventsd-uuid. A change-notification history, not an audit: records are coalesced and logs roll off; there is no timestamp in the format, so event ids give order within one log, not time; a Renamed flag means the path took part in a rename and pairs no old and new name. Only 1SLD and 2SLD pages are read: another page magic (3SLD, say) is reported unsupported with the magic seen and the rest of that file is not decoded. Nothing is guessed or dropped silently: per file the state is parsed, partial, empty, unsupported or failed; per gzip member complete, truncated or failed with its compressed offset; per page parsed, unsupported, invalid length or truncated; per record decoded, empty path or incomplete; bytes that could not be placed in a page are counted and located, and a flag bit with no name is reported as flags_undecoded. status is complete only when every file is parsed or empty, partial when some file was read, and failed when none was (a file in a format the tool does not read is still counted unsupported in files_by_state); status_basis says what it rests on, and every refusal carries both. Decoding is streamed and expansion is capped (max_expanded_bytes per file; a file that hits it is partial and says so). Records are written to out_file (mode 0600) as they are decoded (an existing file or link there is refused); otherwise the page is `limit` records and the whole is in a file under tool-output that the answer names. The inline answer is bounded by bytes (max_inline_bytes) as well as by count, and says so (inline_bounded_by_bytes). Trailing NUL bytes of a page are padding_bytes in the coverage, not records: a record that is all zero is padding, not an empty-path record. A rerun that finds fewer records does not replace a larger earlier page file: it writes a new name and says which it kept. A file of many gzip members is read in linear time (a lookup of the member of a page is a bisect). The tool has a clock of its own, max_seconds (default 200, at most 250, below the 300 seconds of the manifest), read at every record (the record in hand is judged first: a path of 250 KB takes 0.4 second, and the clock was read every 512 records, which ran max_seconds 3 to 12.8 seconds; the answer's sealing, up to 10 seconds, comes after it; the listing of the directory is under the clock too, and the names it did not get to are counted in directory.names_not_examined; the ordering of the files is under it as well): when it passes, the file in hand is closed as partial at the page it was reading (problems names the offset), the files after it are counted not_attempted and the first 2,000 of them listed in per_file (files_not_listed counts the others), time_limit says how to go on, and what was decoded is in the file. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it the same way: one JSON answer with status partial and interrupted set to the signal's name, exit 128 plus the signal, every record already written whole in the file. A stop signal that arrives while the answer is being sealed (up to 10 seconds, with a large preview) waits for the answer and is named in it: interrupted is set, status is partial and the exit code is 128 plus the signal. A signal that arrives while the text of the answer is being made or written (a few tenths of a second for an answer of 20 to 44 MB) cannot be put into a text that is already out: it is found afterwards, the exit code is still 128 plus the signal and stderr says that the answer on stdout is whole and was not marked (before this, 2 of 18 signals sent in that window to knowledgec_query and 2 of 14 to fsevents_parse ended with exit code 0 and an answer that said complete). SIGKILL cannot be handled. contains is a regular expression run only in a restricted subset (at most 256 characters; no back-reference, conditional, lookaround, atomic group or possessive repeat; no repeat of 9 or more inside any repeat, no repeat at all and no alternation inside a repeat of 9 or more; at most two repeats of 9 or more and at most eight repeats of any size; repeats of 2 to 8 inside one another whose counts multiply to more than 16, such as ((((((a?){8}){8}){8}){8}){8}){8}b, which is exponential and passed an earlier subset), refused as JSON with the reason otherwise (a pattern such as (a|aa)+$ took 37 seconds over a path of 40 characters; fourteen such patterns are tested, each refused in milliseconds), and each search runs under a timer of 0.5 second: a path that runs past it is counted in filters.contains_timeouts and the answer is partial. contains is matched against the path as the answer prints it (after the boundary), never against a path or a piece of a path that is withheld, so it cannot be used to test a guess of a withheld name; a record that is not matched and has text withheld in its path is counted in filters.contains_blind_records and the answer is partial, because the needle may be in what is withheld. The count is the same whatever the needle is. The answer says whether a pattern was given, not what it was. SENSITIVE: a path is evidence text and can hold an identifier or a secret (a user or share name, a mail attachment, a token in a file name). WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out, with two checks of the tool's own around it). The windows-forensics pack's shared boundary block, copied byte for byte (a test holds the copies equal), judges every key and value of the answer, of an error answer, and of every row of every file this tool writes, by the type of the field it fills: a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain); free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld; and a second check, written apart from the first, reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token. write_values: true writes the originals of everything the boundary withheld to fsevents_parse-values.jsonl under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants in the path of a record, in a path with an invalid UTF-8 byte (whose bytes are also given as hexadecimal, path_raw_hex) and as the name of a record file (rates, not guarantees; a second measurement planted 1,000 per shape in a path, 200 as a file name, and tests/pack-macos-forensics-boundary.test.ts plants 300 per shape and asserts the bounds). Of the 21 shapes the boundary claims (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google and npm tokens, AWS key ids, JWT, PEM private keys, user-info with an @ in the password, Password= and password: values, NUL and zero-width splits, base64 keys of 16, 20 and 32 bytes, AWS-shaped keys of 40 characters, random base62 of 24 and 40 characters) 20 were printed whole in 0 of 1,000 plants in a path and random base62 of 24 characters in 1 to 2 of 1,000; a piece of 12 characters of an AWS-shaped key was printed in 1 to 3 of 1,000 plants; as the name of a record file base64 keys of 16 bytes in 8 of 200 (4%, where a / is replaced by _). Two checks of the tool's own surround the boundary, which is the windows pack's block and is not edited here: the hexadecimal of a field (path_raw_hex of a path that is not UTF-8, raw_hex of fseventsd-uuid, first_bytes_hex of a file that is not FSEvents) is read once more with the NULs and the invisible characters taken out, in UTF-8 and in UTF-16 (a token cut by a NUL, by an invisible character (format characters, combining marks, private-use and unassigned code points, fillers) or by a control character every 15 characters or fewer shows no run that looks like a secret in the bytes as they are; each control character that occurs in the text is also taken out alone, one at a time, because taking all of them out at once joins the printable bytes of random data into runs; a token cut by two or more different control characters is not read through; a field so long and so full of control characters that this would take over 2 million characters of reading, about 64 KB of random bytes, is withheld), and is withheld when that text holds a secret-shaped run; and a FileVault personal recovery key (six groups of four capitals and digits joined by -) is withheld by a rule of its own. Before them a token cut by zero-width characters in a path with an invalid UTF-8 byte was printed whole in path_raw_hex in 1,000 of 1,000 plants; after them 0 of 200. A token cut by a control character (U+0001, DEL, NEL), a private-use code point every 6 characters was printed whole in path_raw_hex in 200 of 200 plants each and, with U+0001, in raw_hex of fseventsd-uuid in 60 of 60; after the checks 0 of 200 and 0 of 60 (the same token in a text path in 0). The checks' cost, on 300 real file heads of 4 KB (one Mac's /Applications, /System/Library, /usr/lib, /Library and /usr/share): the block alone withholds 113, the checks 6 more (3 before this change); on 300 binary property list heads 178 and 2 more (1 before); on 1,000 random blobs of 256 bytes 0 and 0, of 4 KB 6 and 4 more (0 before); private-use and unassigned code points alone added 0 of 300 and 0 of 1,000. A token written as spaced hexadecimal, as percent escapes, zlib-compressed or reversed is printed in a BLOB's head as it is in a text field (690, 690, 679 and 98 of 690 plants): the boundary does not claim these shapes and the checks do not read them. A FileVault recovery key was printed in 95% of plants as a path component (143 of 150) and in 35% as a file name (60 of 200 plants as the name of a record file); after the rule, which looks for the six groups wherever they stand, also next to other letters or digits, 0 of 300 as a path component, as the file part of a path, in a path with text around it and in a path with an invalid UTF-8 byte, and 0 of 200 as the name of a record file (per_file and problems print the file name with the rule applied). The shapes it does not claim are printed: a plain password, a four-word passphrase and a UUID-shaped key, 1,000 of 1,000; a BitLocker recovery key (eight groups of six digits), 1,000 of 1,000; a random token of 16 characters with spaces or - _ . among them (a Wi-Fi password) in 35 to 67% of plants; random base62 of 16 characters in 0.4 to 1.0%, of 20 in 0.1 to 0.9%, of 32 in 0.1 to 0.2%; text written as spaced characters, as HTML entities, as hexadecimal with spaces or as percent escapes in a text field, 1,000 of 1,000. Costs: on 30,000 paths of a Mac's Library, Applications and /Library outside Library/Caches 3.8% had a component withheld and 2.2% were replaced whole by the second check (the author's 30,658 paths of another corpus: 1.2% and 7.1% of all paths; 31.8% of the 29,342 under Library/Caches, which are hash-named entries); on 30,000 paths of /private/var/folders and cache directories 90.1% (on a sample of 1,000 paths under /private/var/folders of one Mac: all 1,000). The id of a user's temporary folder (/var/folders/xx/ and 30 characters) is shown as an alias of its sha256 (tmp-id- and 12 hexadecimal digits of the sha256 of the id: the same id is the same alias in every run and in every tool, on purpose, so that a path can be followed from one answer to the next, and an id that is guessed can be confirmed by hashing it; the original is in the values file of a secret job) when the block would withhold it: of the same 1,000 paths 176 have text withheld now and 33 are replaced whole (77 before). NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name, random bytes with no text in them, anything under 16 characters in a name): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: path components that are hash-named (cache entries), numbers of 19 digits or more, unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more, and camel-case identifiers of 16 characters or more with no word the block knows. Paths longer than 262,144 characters are cut there and the rest is withheld whole.

path.description: An /.fseventsd directory (its fseventsd-uuid is read as the log's identity; links are not followed), or one record file

contains.description: Case-insensitive regular expression over the path as the answer prints it, in a restricted subset (at most 256 characters; no back-reference, lookaround, atomic group or possessive repeat; no nested or alternated long repeat; repeats of 2 to 8 inside one another may multiply to 16 at most; at most two repeats of 9 or more and eight of any size); refused as JSON otherwise. Each search is given 0.5 second

flags.description: Keep only records carrying one of these flag names, e.g. ["Removed","Renamed"]; a name the tool does not know is listed in filters.flags_unknown

limit.description: Records shown inline (default 2000). All are counted; the whole result is in out_file, or, when that is omitted, in a file under work/<your id>/tool-output/ (in a job, $OUT/tool-output/) that the answer names

out_file.description: JSONL path for every matching record (each row judged by the boundary), written as each is decoded, mode 0600. The tool does not overwrite: an existing file or link at that name is refused

max_expanded_bytes.description: Decompressed bytes read from one file before it stops and says so (default 268435456)

max_page_bytes.description: A page declaring more than this is reported as an invalid page length and not read (default 67108864). A page is held whole while its records are decoded, so memory is several times the largest page read

max_inline_bytes.description: The inline records are cut at this many bytes as well as at `limit` records (default 1048576): the page is the records before the first that does not fit (one path can be megabytes); the whole is in out_file or the file the answer names

max_seconds.description: The tool's own clock (default 200, at most 250): read at every record; when it passes, the file in hand is partial and the files after it are not_attempted, named; a larger value is clamped and the answer says so

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to $OUT/fsevents_parse-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
